Question: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) be real numbers with \(|a - b| = 2,\) \(|b - c| = 3,\) and \(|c - d| = 4.\) What is the sum of all possible values of \(|a - d|?\)
Solution:
Each absolute-value condition allows two signed differences. Since the intermediate terms cancel,
\[
a-d=(a-b)+(b-c)+(c-d)=\pm2\pm3\pm4.
\]
Every combination of signs is attainable: start with \(d=0\), choose \(c\) so that \(c-d=\pm4\), then choose \(b\) so that \(b-c=\pm3\), and finally choose \(a\) so that \(a-b=\pm2\).

Negating all three signed differences negates their sum and preserves its absolute value. Thus it is enough to take the first difference as \(+2\) and check the four choices for the other two:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2+3+4&=9, & 2+3-4&=1,\\
2-3+4&=3, & 2-3-4&=-5.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their absolute values are the four distinct numbers \(1,3,5,9\). The sign-pair argument covers all eight combinations, so there are no other values. Their sum is
\[
1+3+5+9=18,
\]
choice D.
